subject: Soft-commit pilot procurement proposal: temporary PO-lite flow
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@stratify.io>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@stratify.io
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot onboarding & PO requirement question

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to kick off a small pilot (6 weeks) with Stratify.IO. Two quick procurement questions before we sign paperwork:

1) Do you require a formal Purchase Order (PO) for pilots under $20k? Our procurement process is slow and usually wants a PO for anything that touches vendor systems, but for trials they prefer a lightweight process.
2) If a PO is required, is there an alternate path (credit card invoice, short-term soft commitment) that you accept while procurement completes their PO intake?

Attached is our standard onboarding form and the proposed pilot SOW (draft) — we can remove any clauses that create extra procurement overhead. Also, legal asked about liability limits and data handling language.

Can you confirm the minimal evidence you need on your side to route invoices without a PO? If we can do a temporary soft-commit (signed SOW + onboarding form + accounts contact), that would speed the start.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call today.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Stratify.IO
lena.ortiz@stratify.io
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: stratify_onboarding_form.pdf (application/pdf), pilot_statement_of_work.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@stratify.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, accounts@stratify.io
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding & PO requirement question

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the forms.

Short answer: for pilots under $20k we can often avoid a PO if a few conditions are met (this is our temporary "soft-commit" path):
- Signed pilot SOW or equivalent that explicitly states the scope, duration, and estimated spend cap (<= $20,000).
- Completed vendor onboarding form (the one you attached is perfect).
- A named accounts receivable contact (you already cc'd accounts@stratify.io).
- Agreement to our standard 30-day invoice term for pilot invoices.

Operationally: Sales and Finance need to approve the exception. I've looped in Marissa (sales lead on this account) and Priyom (procurement intake) to confirm the internal checks — Marissa, can you confirm we can route via soft-commit here? Priyom, any evidence checklist Finance will want?

Note on legal: anything outside standard Redwood terms (e.g., changes to indemnity, unlimited liability) will require Legal review and may block the soft path. If Stratify wants a lower liability cap or privacy addendum, please flag the line items.

If everyone agrees, we can sign the SOW and treat the first invoice as "pilot invoice" routed to accounts for Net30 without waiting for a PO. That gets you started while procurement completes their PO issuance.

Happy to set a 15-min alignment call this afternoon.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (510) 555-0190

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Diego / Lena — quick note from Sales: we can accept the soft-commit flow for this pilot with two commercial safeguards:

1) Spend cap: pilot capped at $15,000 total (we'll include a line in the SOW).
2) Payment cadence: Redwood to invoice after milestone completion (mid-pilot and end-pilot) with Net30. If Stratify cannot commit to Net30, we can accept a credit card for the first invoice only.

Operational asks for a smooth intake:
- Completed onboarding form (Lena, thanks for the upload).
- PO is optional but preferred long-term; for now Accounts will accept invoices without PO if the SOW includes the cap and AR contact.
- Priyom, can procurement log this as a temporary exception with an expiry (auto-close) after 90 days? We want to avoid indefinite soft-commits.

Link to HubSpot pilot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890 — I'll update the SOW there.

If Parties agree, I can push the redlined SOW to DocuSign today.

—Marissa

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Diego / Marissa — Finance sign-off with conditions below. We can approve a temporary PO-lite/soft-commit path for this specific pilot (DEAL-7892) provided the following are satisfied before the first invoice issues:

1) Pilot spend cap of $15,000 documented in the SOW.
2) Completed vendor onboarding form (we need the W-9 or EU VAT equivalent if applicable).
3) A signed SOW (DocuSign trace) that includes the spend cap and invoice routing instructions to accounts@redwood.ai.
4) Exception duration: this approval is valid for 90 days from the SOW signature; procurement must either close the PO or escalate for an extension.

Legal flags we reviewed: Stratify's draft contains a mutual indemnity clause with unlimited exposure. That must be capped to Redwood's standard (see legal template). If Legal needs to re-redline, the soft-commit is conditional on those edits.

Once those items are in place, Accounts will accept pilot invoices without a formal PO and process Net30. Please attach the onboarding evidence and DocuSign link in the HubSpot record. Priyom, I'll rely on you to record the exception and set the 90-day expiry.

Naomi Feldman
